target.title: Add bulk price update endpoint
target.description:
Lets the pricing team apply a percentage change to every item at once,
for example factor=1.05 for a 5% increase.

summary: Adds a bulk price update endpoint allowing authenticated users to apply a multiplier factor to all item prices.

suspects.title: Missing role authorization check for bulk price update
suspects.problem: The endpoint uses @require_login which permits any logged-in user to change pricing, whereas other destructive or administrative routes like delete_item use @require_role("admin"). This might allow regular users to modify item prices.
suspects.how_to_check: Search the repository for definitions of @require_login and @require_role to see how permissions are enforced and whether pricing modifications should be restricted to admins.

evidence.note: The bulk update prices endpoint uses @require_login instead of @require_role('staff') or @require_role('admin')
Creating an item requires staff role
Deleting an item requires admin role

arguments.explanation: The new endpoint POST /items/bulk-price updates the prices of all items in the catalogue using a multiplier factor supplied in the request body. However, it is protected only by the `@require_login` decorator, which permits any logged-in user (including customers with role rank 'customer') to perform this destructive and administrative catalogue modification. Other item modification and administrative endpoints such as item creation (`@require_role("staff")`), item deletion (`@require_role("admin")`), and export endpoints correctly enforce privileged roles.
arguments.claim: The bulk price update endpoint only requires @require_login instead of an administrative or staff role, allowing any authenticated user to modify prices across the entire item catalogue.
